item.title: Otera-I1 Paradox
item.description:
Infobox The Otera-Interceptor 1 Paradox is a single seat, single engine, light interceptor starfighter manufactured by Sideways Collective Industries. It was the first interceptor design in the Otera starfighter line. The Paradox focused primarily on speed and manoeuvrability rather than firepower, lacking any payloads for its first few renditions. Most Otera-I1s were exclusively sold to military security firms for use in peacekeeping and patrol projects, rather than being available on the open market. Although still popular, the Paradox's limited functionality compared to the Otera-F1 Paradigm meant it did not break any records throughout its lifetime.
The Otera-I1A was the first model of the Paradox available to buyers. It came equipped with a light Cirus GMAT Autocoil and lacked any hardpoints for additional payload capacity. Despite its relatively weak firepower, the I1A's low mass and high thrust meant it boasted a very high acceleration rate for its time. The platform served as the base for many future interceptor developments.One such development was the Otera-I1C, which after the I1B model failed to pass the prototype stage, ended up as the A model's successor. Released in 1779, the Otera-I1C doubled the number of reaction control system piping and thrusters on the vehicle's external layers. This upgrade greatly increased its manoeuvrability.According to communication between SCI employees, consumer feedback demanded a smaller frame for the Otera-I1. Over the decade spanning 1780 to 1790, several prototypes for the next Paradox were considered. Due to various concerns with conflicting systems and the safety of module positioning, most of the models failed to make it past the blueprinting stage. The Otera-I1E and I1H models nearly made it to production, but several RCS failures during testing caused them to be redesigned yet again.The primary issue faced by SCI engineers was the positioning of RCS piping against other modules, especially near the tail where fuel tanks and combustion systems needed be stored in high pressure environments. During flight, the force experienced by these systems when the thrusters of either type were engaged for too long meant a rupture somewhere along the pipelines could occur.The Otera-I1J solved this problem by separating the central RCS fuel zone into separate sections, each supplied with their own storage of fuel. Although this meant that different RCS zones could deplete their fuel at different rates, the change removed the need for additional piping throughout the starship, freeing up additional space for the rest of the modules despite the total reduction in size. The I1J reduced the Paradox's physical size by 20%.The Otera-I1K came out shortly after the I1J, continuing the acquired momentum of development. It added 15 more countermeasures, for a total of 45, and reduced the countermeasure packet size to 1. In addition, the main engine was upgraded to the new standard.
The Otera-I1L was the final rendition of the Paradox, and introduced two M-CX missile hardpoints to the wingtips. No radar was mounted to the platform due to the limited space, meaning it was limited to infrared tracking missiles. Given the Paradox's interceptor role, additional ordnance was never considered for the starfighter. The I1L was typically equipped with not yet converted SLAM-4 infrared missiles.
Starfighters

item.title: QLA-E1
item.description:
Infobox The Quick-Launch A Edition 1 rocket was developed by Topman Dynamics as a baseline design for general purpose high explosive rockets. Featuring a Quick-Launch system, it could be fired from a rocket pod at a moment’s notice, allowing for improved accuracy and an overall greater effectiveness. The primary drawback of the QLA-E1 was that is was built upon the ageing Razor rocket model. It has thus been replaced by the QLA-E2 and QLB-E4 rockets, but the QLA-E1 remains in production with Primus Manufacturing and is still used today, although only as a training device for new pilots.
Rockets

item.title: Razor
item.description:
Infobox The Razor was a single thruster, high explosive rocket designed and manufactured by Bleak Enterprise. It saw extensive use during the Cosmian Wars, but was ultimately pulled from factories at the end of the conflicts and was never continued by other companies. The QLA-E1 utilised several leftover Razor units as the shells for its prototypes.
Rockets

item.title: QLA-E2
item.description:
Infobox The Quick-Launch A Edition 2 rocket was developed by Topman Dynamics as a continuation of the QLA-E1. For this rendition of the rocket, the high explosive warhead was swapped out for an armour piercing type for use against armoured targets. The E2 also improved upon the internal separation system in order to optimise the release-and-launch process. Unlike other models of its family, the QLA-E2 is no longer produced in Primus Manufacturing's facilities.
Rockets

item.title: QLB-E4
item.description:
Infobox The Quick-Launch B Edition 4 rocket was developed by Topman Dynamics as a direct upgrade of the QLA-E1 released 47 years earlier. It returned to the original high explosive warhead type equipped by the E1 while also incorporating the various changes made with the QLA-E2 rocket. Despite its age, the QLB-E4 still serves as the base for modern standard space rockets and is presently manufactured by Primus Manufacturing.
Rockets

item.title: Bombs
item.description:
Bombs are a type of explosive ordnance ammunition lacking forward propulsion dropped or guided onto a surface target such as a vehicle or structure. They come with varying amounts of explosive mass, denoted by their relative explosive class, which ranges from 1 (approx. 250 kg equivalent) to 6 (approx. 4000 kg). Although the stereotypical classic bomb is unguided, modern bombs are often guided by laser or by satellite. None
PG Diver
UGP Jerami

item.title: UGP Jerami
item.description:
Infobox The Unguided General Purpose is a series of light unguided bombs designed by Topman Dynamics and manufactured by Primus Manufacturing for use by starships in both training and combat scenarios. Fitted with protective shielding to prevent space debris from damaging the bomb's outer shell as well as a safe fuse, the UGP series is used as a modern standard for explosive classes and space-friendly design.
The UGP - Revision 1 Jerami is a light bomb of explosive class 1 primarily used for training Kolban Alliance starfighter pilots in live fire exercises. Its small size and low mass make it desirable for limiting effects on torque when carrying asymmetrical payloads in controlled environments. Revisions 2 and 3 use the same model, but increase size, mass and explosive class.
The UGP - Revision 4 was a heavy bomb of explosive class 4 used by various militaries in indiscriminate bombing operations. It was developed off of the previous revisions of the UGP series. The UGP-R4 is no longer used and was replaced by modern guided ammunition.
Bombs

item.title: PG Diver
item.description:
Infobox The Pinpoint Guidance Diver is a laser-guided bomb designed by Payne Explotech for use by starships. Its custom integrated targeting system allows it to hit targets within a few metres of the specified target location from dropping distances of more than eight kilometres. The Diver uses a combination of four reaction control system thrusters to affect its flight path as well as an internal reaction wheel to make minor angling adjustments. Although more modern versions have been released, the bomb remains in use in the present day and continues to be manufactured by Primus Manufacturing.
The PG1 Diver I was the first Diver to be released in 2056. A powerful bomb of explosive class 5, it was used extensively by various militaries. However, production of the Diver I was ceased after the creation of the PG2.
The PG2 Diver II is an explosive class 5 bomb currently in service with the Kolban Alliance and several organisations. It introduced an improved set of reaction control thrusters, as well as infrared and ultraviolet shielding to prevent system damage during flight.
The PG2-S Diver S was a miniaturised version of the PG2 Diver II. Featuring the same systems but with a reduced size and an explosive class of 3 instead of the usual 5, the Diver S was introduced to the market in response to the Human military's request for increased customisability of their starship payloads.The PG3 Diver III is the newest rendition of the Diver series, having its explosive class increased to 6. Although most aspects of the bomb were upgraded with the PG3, a high price tag has prevented it from gaining enough traction beyond the Kolban Alliance.
Bombs

item.title: Satellites
item.description: Satellites are orbital structures used for many different applications where automation or remote control is a necessary or helpful method. These applications include but are not limited to the collection of various types of data on a particular topic, or assisting with the transmission of data alongside Long Range Transmission Ports (LRTP). None None - Will be added in a dedicated database update

item.title: SecTac CRG
item.description:
Infobox The Secondary Tactical Conventional Range Grenade is a range grenade designed by Payne Explotech and manufactured by Primus Manufacturing. Purposed for use by security staff or military personnel, the SecTac is fired out of coilgun secondary grenade launchers. It is also armed with a safe fuse intended to prevent misfires and make the weapon safer for its users, without impeding on its effectiveness. This safe fuse can be loaded with both lethal and stun charges.
Range Grenades

item.title: Range Grenades
item.description:
Not to be confused with infantry equipment explosives, range grenades are a type of soft light ammunition fired out of conventional weapons that explode on contact with the ground. None
SecTac CRG

item.title: PBC-Ex Shell
item.description:
Infobox The Plasma-Based Composite Experimental Shell was a dedicated artillery strike shell designed for use against lone, individual targets. Originally designed by Harry's Heatworks with the support of Primus Manufacturing, it was the first projectile specifically designed to utilise plasma in a long range attack role. The shell was utilised by the PAC ONE Midnight Comet and PAC TWO Azure Meteor artillery units.
Shells

item.title: PAC ONE Midnight Comet
item.description:
Infobox The Plasma Accelerator Complex ONE Midnight Comet was the first artillery cannon to make use of plasma-based composite shells, a newly released highly reactive and damaging projectile. The PBC-Ex Shell, designed as a joint project between Primus Manufacturing and Harry's Heatworks, was the primary experimental projectile fired by the Midnight Comet.
The unit itself came from a long line of military weapons designed by the anonymous Granule Reduction, and was picked up for production by Harry's Heatworks, the company well known for its variety of industrial applications of plasma. Artillery units making use of the PAC ONE saw moderate success in its operation, although some major flaws, such as an unreliable plasma moderation system made it undesirable for most. The PAC ONE is no longer manufactured, with the much safer PAC TWO Azure Meteor replacing it.
Artillery

item.title: Shells
item.description:
Shells are explosive projectiles designed to be fired out of cannons, whether as part of artillery or from ground vehicles. Unlike bullets, shells do not have a particular classification system, although there are various different types of shells that have specific purposes.
PriMa Heavy Shell - A series of artillery strike shells under mass production with Primus Manufacturing
PBC-Ex Shell
PriMa Heavy Shell

item.title: PriMa Heavy Shell
item.description:
Infobox The Primus Manufacturing Heavy Shell is a series of dedicated artillery shells mass produced by ammunition manufacturing company Primus Manufacturing. It consists of several different types of shells, each designed for a particular purpose in battle.
Shells

item.title: Bullets
item.description:
Bullets are the most common type of ammunition and consist of the projectiles usually fired out of coilguns. There are many different types of bullets, each with their own sizes and shapes. For the purpose of usage in coilgun systems, bullets are typically produced using ferromagnetic iron and nickel. The vast majority of bullets are manufactured and developed by Primus Manufacturing.Common bullets are generally referred to with the designation of Class-##(#). The first ## refers to the shape of the bullet. The shape of a bullet depends on how it is being used: AA for Anti-Aircraft, AS for Anti-Starship, AG for Anti-Ground Vehicle, IW for Infantry Weaponry, PA for Planetary Aircraft vehicles and SA for Starship Armaments. There is occasionally crossover between classes, with specific sizes being equivalent between them.The second # refers to the size of the bullet. The size of a bullet again depends on how it is being used. In order of largest to smallest: A, B, C, D, W, X, Y, Z. Sizes Z and Y are typically used for light arms, such as sidearms and light vehicle armaments. X and W are typically used for rifles and medium vehicle armaments. D and C are usually used for cycler coilguns, sniper coilguns and heavy vehicle armaments. B and A are primarily reserved for superheavy coilguns and non-explosive coilcannons. Although these are the recommended usages, it is possible and not uncommon to use different bullet sizes in alternative ways.
Not all bullets are singular projectiles. They can also exist as shotgun shells, which instead of firing as an individual solid object, are torn apart upon exiting the barrel and fly as multiple smaller projectiles. The most common of these is the Standard Shotgun Shell.

item.title: Class-SA Bullet
item.description:
Infobox The Class-SA Bullet is a high velocity, multipurpose coilgun projectile designed to be fired from the main armaments of starships (primarily starfighters). They can be used against both other starships as well as against larger or more armoured targets, such as orbital structures. SA bullets are mass produced by Primus Manufacturing.
Bullets

item.title: Class-PA Bullet
item.description:
Infobox The Class-PA Bullet is a high velocity, multipurpose coilgun projectile designed to be fired from the main armaments of aircraft. They can be used against both other aircraft as well as against ground targets. PA bullets are mass produced by Primus Manufacturing.
Bullets

item.title: MC3C Zircon
item.description:
Infobox The Mejir & Cron 3C "Zircon" is a light cycler coilgun and the third product designed independently by the Mejir & Cron weapons manufacturing company. A slow firing but hard hitting light cycler thanks to its use of the IW(W) bullet, the Zircon favours precision and low numbers of targets over the common "spray and pray" tactic often employed with oppositely oriented cycler coilguns.Consumers were pleased with the cycler's manageable recoil and accuracy, but felt that the weapon was too massive and unwieldy to use in active combat. This led to the Zircon's general use as a supporting coilgun rather than as a frontline fighter. Although it filled in a somewhat small niche, the MC3C was very popular with those who used it.
Primary Arms

item.title: Class-IW Bullet
item.description:
Infobox The Class-IW Bullet is a low velocity, basic coilgun projectile designed to be fired from various infantry equipment including primary arms and sidearms. Ballistic capping on the tips of the bullet is helps to penetrate the relatively thin body armour worn by infantry. IW bullets are mass produced by Primus Manufacturing.
Bullets

item.title: Class-AG Bullet
item.description:
Infobox The Class-AG Bullet is a high velocity, heavy armour piercing coilgun projectile designed to penetrate the typically thick armour used by ground vehicles. AG bullets are mass produced by Primus Manufacturing.
Bullets

item.title: Class-AS Bullet
item.description:
Infobox The Class-AS Bullet is a high velocity, armour piercing coilgun projectile designed to penetrate both the defensive electromagnetic field and armour used by starships. AS bullets are mass produced by Primus Manufacturing.
Bullets

item.title: Class-AA Bullet
item.description:
Infobox The Class-AA Bullet is a semi-armour piercing coilgun projectile designed to penetrate the thin armour used by most high speed atmospheric aircraft, before detonating within the airframe. AA bullets are mass produced by Primus Manufacturing.
Bullets

item.title: Civilian Ships
item.description:
Civilian ships are non-combative, non-military starships, designed for use by members of the general public, either for personal use or as part of an organisations. Due to their nature as privately owned property, most civilian ships are designed with a greater focus on outward style. None
SCI-700 Forrester

item.title: Civilian Aircraft
item.description:
Civilian aircraft are non-combative, non-military airborne vehicles and devices owned and operated by members of the public, whether for personal use or as part of an organisation. As such, most civilian aircraft focus more on style and looks rather than only on function and purpose. None
SCI-144 Pipette

item.title: Support Ships
item.description:
Support ships are a range of unarmed specialised starships designed to carry out particular tasks, such as mining, carrying starfighters, or even serving as a mobile hospital platform.
VSM-02 - A light miner support ship designed and manufactured by Vleil Starworks

item.title: VSM-01
item.description:
Infobox The Vleil Starworks Miner-01 was a two seat, triple engine, light miner support ship designed and manufactured by Vleil Starworks for the Dottian government. It utilised a set of three external mining drills in order to extract minerals from asteroid belts and comets. Similarly to the VSM-00, an magnetic plate was used to collect these extracted materials. The VSM-01 was one of the longest continuously serving starships in the history of the Dottian star fleet, being produced from its release in 204 CE to its retirement in 576 CE.
Support Ships

item.title: VSM-02
item.description:
Infobox The Vleil Starworks Miner-02 was a single seat, triple engine, light miner support ship designed and manufactured by Vleil Starworks for the Dottian government. It made use of the same three drills and magnetic plating as the VSM-01, but due to a rising demand for increased strip mining of asteroid fields, introduced the use of controlled explosives. A mechanical arm for placing the explosive charges in a safe and precise manner was included with the VSM-02, positioned on the top of the fuselage.
Support Ships

item.title: VSS-00
item.description:
Infobox The Vleil Starworks Scavenger-00 was a single seat, single engine, light scavenger support ship designed and manufactured by Vleil Starworks for the Dottian government. Designed to search the wreckages of destroyed starships for recyclable valuable materials, the VSS-00 is equipped with a three-fingered robotic clamping device as well as a basic collection unit. An existing restored VSS-00 unit is located at the Kolban Technology History Museum.
Support Ships

item.title: Metallist
item.description:
Infobox Metallists are insect lithotrophic creatures that reside on the deserts of Totto. With pure minerals as their main diet, they have incredibly strong mandibles and teeth allowing them to cut through thin sheets of steel. Metallists are infamous for the high pitched screeching sound they produce when cutting through metal or hard rocks.Metallists make use of incredibly sharp and jagged mandibles, partially made out of the metals they consume to mechanically digest various rocks and minerals. These mandibles curve around the front of their head, which sits ahead of the rest of their mostly rectangular body. Their six legs feature thick, stubby ends to accommodate for the sandy surface they frequently travel across.Metallists are primarily swarm insects, acting together in groups of up to tens of thousands. An individual Metallist will only eat approximately 2 grams of material over the course of two days, but together in their colonies, this can amount to up to 100 kilograms of consumed mass in a week for a particularly large group. Metallists have been observed consuming parts of a starship, indicating a lack of regard for the type of metal they consume. They will usually ignore any organic matter they encounter but in the event of an attack can be easily killed or scared off by small flames. Metallists are very fearful of all kinds of fire and will avoid it at all costs, even if their meal is nearby.
Fauna
Nature

item.title: SCS-1 Blackout
item.description:
Infobox The Sideways Collective Stealthbomber 1 Blackout is a two seat, triple engine, stealth oriented tactical superbomber starfighter manufactured by Sideways Collective Industries for the Kolban Alliance. Designed to infiltrate deep into enemy territory with minimal detection, the SCS-1 is the result of the culmination of many of Topman Dynamics' experimental stealth designs, from radar shielding to automatic signal regulation systems. It carries a large payload, with 80 B-C4 class hardpoints hidden within a closed bomb bay capable of carrying most kinds of explosive ordnance. The payload quantity, however, is limited by the size of the bombs themselves, so only bombs of explosive class 3 or below can match the maximum number. The Blackout is seldom deployed and as such many of its missions remain classified. According to the project leads at Topman Dynamics, the development process of the SCS-1 is "still ongoing".
Starfighters

item.title: Otera-S1 Nightlighter
item.description:
Infobox The Otera-Superbomber 1 Nightlighter is a two seat, triple engine, superbomber starfighter manufactured by Sideways Collective Industries. It was designed as a replacement for the Otera-B1 Sorcerer, the development of which had recently ceased. Demand for superbombers had increased in recent years and the Nightlighter was intended to fill the gap. Easily identifiable by its short and wide shape, the Otera-S1 had a unique design intended to make it less visually identifiable, a technique utilised centuries later in the design of the SCS-1 Blackout. The Nightlighter infamously had no defensive armament besides 600 countermeasures.
The Otera-S1A was the first and only public rendition of the Nightlighter, as the funding for the project was never renewed after its initial release. It came with a total of 20 hardpoints, giving it a considerable amount of firepower. The 600 countermeasure count helped the starship to defend itself, but when facing a close range battle with coilguns, it lost most of its advantages.The Otera-S1T was an experimental continuation of the starship's development in 1800, that never passed the initial prototype stage. It trialled the use of additional bomb racks in order to increase the total payload of the ship. There were plans in the blueprints to incorporate a newly designed coilgun system into the Nightlighter, but this never occurred, even in the S1T.
Starfighters

item.title: Starfighters
item.description:
Starfighters are lightweight starships designed for combat in open space. They are typically military-owned, but can also be privately owned for personal use, similarly to a civilian vehicle.
Otera-F1X Deiknunai - The Otera-F1 Paradigm modernisation starfighter released by Sideways Collective Industries in celebration of its 400th anniversary
Otera-B1 Sorcerer
Otera-B1FM Sorcerer
Otera-F1 Paradigm
Otera-F1X Deiknunai
Otera-I1 Paradox

item.title: Otera-F1X Deiknunai
item.description:
Infobox The Otera-Fighter 1X Deiknunai is a single seat, twin engine, light fighter starfighter manufactured by Sideways Collective Industries. It was released as part of the 400th anniversary celebrations of the release of the first Otera line starships. Although almost completely ceremony-focused in practical design, the Deiknunai was designed in line with modern combative starfighter standards, with the exception of stealth capabilities. It comes equipped with the original four B/R/M-CX hardpoints first seen on the Otera-F1C as well as 120 countermeasure packets, combined with a powerful AESA spectral scanning radar.
Starfighters

item.title: Support Aircraft
item.description:
Support aircraft include any military airborne device used to carry out utility tasks. These tasks can range from transportation of troops to surveillance and atmospheric monitoring. None
CT-10 Bluebird
UROS-1 Birdeye

item.title: UROS-1 Birdeye
item.description:
Infobox The Unmanned Reconnaissance, Observation and Surveillance - 1 Birdeye is a reconnaissance drone used to capture images and video of military points of interest. Produced by Sideways Collective Industries, the Birdeye supports the use of night-vision, thermal and ultra-high definition imaging. It is designed with a low profile in order to be able to penetrate enemy territory and producing intelligence that would otherwise be inaccessible. For one mission, the small drone is able to fly for several hours at a time and can be remotely controlled from up to 150 km away. In the event of a system failure or capture, the UROS-1 is also able to remotely self-destruct after transmitting its collected data. The Kolban Alliance artillery division also uses the drone for long-range optical targeting with long range artillery pieces, such as the OSSR-1.
Support Aircraft

item.title: Combat Aircraft
item.description:
Combat aircraft assume the role of performing air-to-air combat, air-to-ground strikes and air-to-space attacks. They are at the forefront of air-based technological development. Modern combat aircraft usually specialise in speed, manoeuvrability, stealth and payload - focusing on quick, powerful attacks and avoiding enemy weapons altogether. None
LAC-1 Vulture

item.title: Civilian Structures
item.description:
Civilian structures include a wide range of key infrastructure owned and operated by non-combative groups. They are commonly designed for a particular purpose, such as the collection of a resource or the monitoring of an area.
SEG-S3 - A second generation soup extraction gate designed by Mansteid Auto
SED Platform
SEG-S1
SEG-S3
SEG-S4

item.title: SEG-S4
item.description:
Infobox The Soup Extraction Gate - Series 4 is a third generation soup extraction gate designed by Mansteid Auto to replace the SEG-S3. It further decreased the minimum crew size while also increasing efficiency. Several materials were swapped out with cheaper alternatives without compromising the integrity or safety of the platform. The resulting reduction in cost and crew allowed the SEG-S4 to become even more accessible.
Civilian Structures

item.title: SEG-S3
item.description:
Infobox The Soup Extraction Gate - Series 3 is a second generation soup extraction gate. After a second design was almost patented but cancelled in the beginning of the Cosmian Wars, Mansteid Auto waited until after the wars to continue its development. However, the excruciatingly long duration of the Cosmian Wars and the immense technological advancements throughout meant that a new one would have to be fully designed from scratch. The SEG-S3 features a more efficient harvesting system than its predecessor as well as a smaller required crew size.
Civilian Structures

item.title: MSEG-S4
item.description:
Infobox The Mobile Soup Extraction Gate - Series 4 is the first mobile design of the SEG family of soup extraction gates. A moderately sized platform with an unusually low crew size, the ability to manoeuvre a soup extraction gate independently proved to be revolutionary in the soup harvesting scene, attracting thousands of buyers. The designer of the SEG family of vehicles and structures, Mansteid Auto, has confirmed that they will cease production of the MSEG-S4 in 2180.
Civilian Vehicles

item.title: SEG-S1
item.description:
Infobox The Soup Extraction Gate - Series 1 is a first generation medium soup extraction gate designed by Mansteid Auto. Capable of harvesting large amounts of soup in a shorter amount of time than conventional drills, the SEG-S1 has been known to have been employed by governments and criminals alike. The only significant drawback to its design is the required crew size, sitting at an unusually high 16. It has since been replaced by more advanced SEG platforms, such as the SEG-S3 and MSEG-S4.
Civilian Structures

item.title: Civilian Vehicles
item.description:
Civilian vehicles include a range of transit technology used by non-military consumers and businesses to transport themselves from location to location. The classification is broad, and can include any type of vehicle from cars, trucks and trains to mobile mining platforms.
MSEG-S4 - A mobile soup extraction gate provided by Mansteid Auto
Farracchi
MSEG-S4

item.title: PAC TWO Azure Meteor
item.description:
Infobox The Plasma Accelerator Complex TWO Azure Meteor is an improved rendition of the PAC ONE Midnight Comet, which had been designed by Granule Reduction. Several changes were made to the original by Harry's Heatworks. The vast majority of the enhancements involved the patching of the various flaws that had greatly brought down the performance of the PAC ONE. These safety improvements also cleared up room for additional performance, increasing the weapon's fire rate and almost doubling its range.
Artillery

item.title: OSSR-1 Usurper I
item.description:
Infobox The Out-of-Sight Shell Repeater 1 Usurper I is the first development of the Fox Corporation's Out-of-Sight Shell Repeater artillery series. Designed by Topman Dynamics and a relatively advanced artillery unit for its time, the sudden arrival of the Usurper on battlefields marked a turning point for surface combat. Capable of accurately hitting targets at extremely long ranges out of sight of the naked eye, the Usurper I is used in combination with drones and advanced targeting technology in order to be aimed.
The OSSR-1 was the first modern portable artillery unit capable of firing shells out of clips, allowing for the rapid bombardment of targets. A single clip contains three shells. The fastest time ever to achieve firing all three shells from an Usurper’s clip stands at 7.23 seconds and was achieved during a Cindus live fire exercise.
The most notable event involving the Usurper I was during a short war between a criminal Dottian militant group and the Human military, in which three lone Usurpers and a strike aircraft defeated an entire criminal battalion escorting a planetary supercannon, without sustaining any friendly casualties.
Artillery

item.title: Support Vehicles
item.description:
Support vehicles are the main ground utility force of an organisation or military. They carry out any required assistive tasks, from transportation of armoured troops to extensive minesweeping of battlefields. Battalions of support vehicles do not take part in fighting and will usually remain far behind the combative force until needed.
USTV-S2 Guppler II - An uncrewed transportation vehicle designed and manufactured by Mansteid Auto
USTV-S1 Guppler
USTV-S2 Guppler II

item.title: USTV-S2 Guppler II
item.description:
Infobox The Unmanned Storage and Transport Vehicle - Series 2 Guppler II is an upgraded model of the USTV-S1 Guppler. Featuring increased modulation capability, an improved engine for faster speeds over rough terrain as well as personnel transportation, Mansteid Auto's CEO advertised the Guppler II as a "significant technological step in the ground vehicles industry". The USTV-S2 is currently the record holder for the most sales of a ground vehicle in its first two weeks of production.
Support Vehicles

item.title: USTV-S1 Guppler
item.description:
Infobox The Unmanned Storage and Transport Vehicle - Series 1 Guppler is a small, unmanned hovercraft support vehicle designed by Mansteid Auto's private sector to carry and transport large amounts of cargo over all kinds of terrain. The Guppler uses specialised navigation AI to follow its designated target (being either another vehicle or location) or can be programmed to follow a predetermined path independently. Capable of being modified to operate in various environments and climates, the vehicle is used by both civilian companies and military organisations. Although spacious, the Guppler does not support the transportation of personnel.
Support Vehicles

item.title: Mark 3
item.description:
Infobox The Mark 3 was the first fully mass-produced tank designed by Grenund Constructive, having passed the examinations performed by Cindus officials to become the new primary tank of the Cindus military. The medium tank featured a new hull and armour layout previously designed for the Mark 2.1 STP, but kept the engine first seen on the Mark 2. Another notable change came in the form of a new cannon, increasing its calibre by 2 millimetres with the 37mm Mark 2 Cannon.
Despite still being relatively simple in terms of its technology, the Mark 3 very quickly proved itself to be potent in battle, soon racking up a consistent weekly kill count. However, when data reports were analysed, it was found that despite the damage the tank was dealing, the Cindus military was still losing a large number of Mark 3 tanks to not just enemy fire, but also frequent breakdowns and fuel shortages.
Combat Vehicles

item.title: Mark 2.1 STP
item.description:
Infobox The Mark 2.1 Survivability Test Prototype was Grenund Constructive's extension of the Mark 2 medium tank, which experimentally reshaped the hull while also further upgrading the armour thickness. This armour redesign meant the Mark 1 and Mark 2 could not be easily converted. However, it did have the desirable capabilities that the Cindii were looking for, and the government funded the next tank
Primitive padding was inserted into some of the crew compartments in order to increase crew comfort, but it was later noted that this did not have the expected effect, instead cramping personnel more due to the reduced size of the hull. The Mark 2.1 never saw combat, but remained in "active" service before being converted to the new Mark 3.
Combat Vehicles

item.title: Mark 2
item.description:
Infobox The Mark 2 was a medium tank designed and manufactured by Grenund Constructive based on the Mark 1. It upgraded the armour all around the tank and reduced the size of some flat surfaces. Although some modules such as the engine received improvements, the majority of the technology within the tank remained unchanged. One coaxial Mark 1 Light Cycler Coilgun was added to the turret beside the main gun, operated by a fifth crew member.
The Cindus military showed some interest in the developing design, although they refused to purchase additional units. However, Grenund Constructive was unable to continue its momentum due to a lack of funding, so the Cindus government offered to hire them on contract.
Combat Vehicles

item.title: Mark 1
item.description:
Infobox The Mark 1 was the first tank designed and manufactured independently by Grenund Constructive. Constructed with very basic materials and technology, the Mark 1 was not as successful as the company had hoped. Even the Cindus military, the would-be primary buyer, opted to prioritise infantry equipment over the underperforming tank after seeing it in tests. In battle, the Mark 1 immediately showed its inferiority to other tanks of the times.Despite its medium classification, the Mark 1's armour was relatively thin, providing as little as 14 millimetres of thickness in some parts. The tank's large size meant it still struggled to keep pace, with a maximum forward speed of 20 kilometres per hour and a reverse speed of only 5 km/h. For most, its only redeeming quality was the fast loading and hard hitting 35mm Mark 1 Cannon mounted in the turret. Unfortunately, this was still brought down by the turret's slow traversal, which was managed by a hand crank operated by the gunner.
Combat Vehicles

item.title: Himms Mk2 SR WRR
item.description:
Infobox The Himms Mk2 Short Range Radio Receiver is a short range communications device named after its original patenter Ian Himms, intended for general use within planetary and starship environments. An improvement over the previous Mk1 design, the Mk2 Receiver featured a significantly longer clear transmission range, overall cleaner transmissions and better transmission security. Overseeing of the manufacturing of the Himms Mk2 during its lifetime has been passed from Lance Innovations to Bleak Enterprise and eventually to the Fox Corporation, which manages it to this day.
Tools

item.title: Infantry Equipment
item.description:
Infantry Equipment is the variety of technology used by both individual military troops during operations and individual personnel part of an organisation that requires some amount of security. It can range from coilguns such as rifles to support tools such as military-grade rations. The current leading infantry equipment manufacturers include the Fox Corporation, Plurge Weapon Solutions, Red Herrings and KunaiTech, among others.
FURLA - An urban carbine rifle coilgun produced by the Fox Corporation
MC1A Sawed Off Shorty - A miniaturised double-barrel shotgun designed and manufactured by Mejir & Cron
ST-Zeal - A heavy duty survival knife produced by SharpTack
KJDT-1L "Killjoy" - An autonomous deployable turret in production with Matchik Technologies
TEMP-SR-10 - An EMP grenade designed by Topman Dynamics and manufactured by the Fox Corporation
SA-FER Protective HazMat Suit - A full-body hazardous materials produced and used by Frank's Fission and Fusion
SuperVision B100 AWB - High power binoculars manufactured by SuperVision Inc.

item.title: KT-Tx
item.description:
Infobox The KunaiTech - Toxic is a lightweight throwing knife developed and manufactured by KunaiTech for general use in combat. Another controversial product from the company, the KT-Tx makes use of a toxin injection vein to insert substances into the target's body. Although the weapon was originally intended to only carry sleeping agents, the injection mechanism supports almost any kind of liquid of the right viscosity. As such, there were concerns from regulators regarding the possible use of the weapon to carry potentially harmful or even lethal substances in place of the default. In 2171, a terrorist attempted to smuggle liquid explosives into governmental facilities on Lister using a KT-Tx, reigniting the discussion on the classification of the weapon.
Deployables

item.title: KT-Fm
item.description:
Infobox The KunaiTech - Flame is a lightweight throwing knife developed and manufactured by KunaiTech for general use in combat. The weapon contains a volatile and flammable liquid that is set alight when the tip of the knife shatters, causing a small focused explosion, very similarly to the HEAT charge commonly used against tanks.
The KT-Fm was initially advertised as a deployable weapon in kind with the other KunaiTech products during its first release. However, a controversy was sparked when experts pointed out that the single use and inherently explosive nature of the knife meant it should be classified instead as an explosive weapon instead. Others were quick to add that its use of fire meant it should be considered a incendiary explosive. This reclassification meant it was required to follow a different and much stricter set of the Kolban Alliance's weapons regulations, significantly limiting the allowed use and manufacture of the product.
Explosives

item.title: KT-Sh
item.description:
Infobox The KunaiTech - Shock is a lightweight throwing knife developed and manufactured by KunaiTech for general use in combat. It uses stored electrical energy in order deliver a painful and sometimes paralysing shock upon piercing a target. Since its release, the KT-Sh has experienced limited manufacture, primarily due to its high cost. This has made it more of a collector's item rather than a weapon in most consumers' eyes.
Deployables

item.title: Explosives
item.description:
Explosives are manufactured support weapons commonly part of a set of infantry equipment that can by used to clear or disable large areas and groups of enemies. The majority of explosives used by infantry are handheld grenades that can be tossed into dangerous areas. Although similar in nature, explosives and deployables are differentiated by the duration of their use, with explosives usually only being single-use.

item.title: Deployables
item.description:
Deployables, oftentimes part of a set of infantry equipment, are tools able to be thrown into or set up in the middle of combat for the purpose of either repeated or medium to long-term use. The most common and easily recognisable type of deployable is the automated attack turret, although there are various different types utilised for a plethora of unique purposes. Given the exact nature of some deployables, they are often at the forefront of technological progression. This comes as a result of the needs or requirements they must fulfil, such as accurate target acquisition and tracking.
KJDT-1H "Killjoy" - An autonomous defence turret produced by Matchik Technologies
KT-Sh - A KunaiTech kunai that uses stored electrical energy to deliver a paralysing shock to its target

KJDT-1L Killjoy

item.title: KT-St
item.description:
Infobox The KunaiTech - Standard is a standard lightweight throwing knife developed and manufactured by KunaiTech for general use in combat. Originally a publicly funded project by the small startup company, the KT-St allowed KunaiTech to expand into additional areas of technological development and become self-sustaining. Although the kunai design was in no way revolutionary or popular with military groups due to their general lack of practical use in combat against considerably more lethal weapons, the frequent content creation surrounding it generated a significant boost in sales with private buyers.
Deployables

item.title: Tools
item.description:
A tool is a general piece of equipment used by infantry both during and outside of active combat. Though not directly utilised for offensive or defensive purposes, they assist the person in carrying out other duties, increasing capability and efficiency.
Himms Mk2 SR WRR - A short range wireless radio communications device designed by Lance Innovations and now manufactured by the Fox Corporation

Himms Mk2 SR WRR

item.title: Himms Mk1 SR WRR
item.description:
Infobox The Himms Mk1 Short Range Wireless Radio Receiver was a short range communications device intended for general use within both planetary and starship environments. Developed by Ian Himms in Lance Innovations, the device became famous for its rugged durability and consistent reliability. The Mk1 version ceased manufacturing once an improved Mk2 design was released.
Tools

item.title: BE Basic Combat Vest
item.description:
Infobox The Bleak Enterprise Basic Combat Vest was a cheap, mass produced kevlar vest for general use. Issued primarily to Bleak Enterprise's own security staff, personnel were not pleased with its performance. In various interviews conducted during the investigation into the company's treatment of employees and history of safety concerns near the end of its life, many staff were quick to point out the vest's limited reliability. Claims of underperformance and even complete failure were not uncommon, with the vest sometimes completely failing to stop even small calibre rounds from puncturing it.
Body Armour

item.title: Body Armour
item.description:
Body Armour is manufactured protective infantry equipment designed to be worn by personnel in combative or otherwise dangerous areas. The exact purpose of it can vary, with some products not intended for use in firefights but rather as protection against passive threats, such as nuclear radiation or general biohazards. Body armour is generally rated by the Kolban Alliance in a dimensionless numbering system, with 0 rated body armour providing little to no additional protection over simple cotton or nylon clothing and 10 rated body armour being almost completely impervious to small arms fire.

item.title: Himms, Ian
item.description:
Infobox Ian Himms patented the original design of the Himms Mk1 Short Range Wireless Radio Receiver, which went on to become a centrepiece for the short range communications industry. The device was not his only original invention, but it was by far his most popular and overshadowed the majority of his other achievements. One of these achievements was the Human's contribution to the design of the third generation series of interstellar communications system.
People

item.title: SuperVision B100 AWB
item.description:
Infobox The SuperVision B100 All-Weather Binoculars are eight-times magnification binoculars designed and manufactured by SuperVision Incorporated for use in hunting and military settings.
Tools
